extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house IP counsel, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Practical overview of defenses and litigation strategies available in U.S. utility patent litigation, including substantive defenses (non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, etc.), procedural and parallel-proceeding tactics, damages and willfulness considerations, and settlement factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-infringement (all-elements rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The accused product or process does not infringe because it does not meet every element of any asserted patent claim (the all-elements rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies include identifying missing claim elements, arguing for a narrow claim construction, technically distinguishing the accused product from the claimed invention, and using prosecution history to limit claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent invalidity (patentability defenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defenses based on failure to meet patentability requirements under U.S. law (e.g., §§101, 102, 103, 112 and improper inventorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common theories: §101 subject-matter ineligibility (Alice/Mayo), §102 anticipation (single prior reference discloses all claim elements), §103 obviousness (combination of references), §112 written description/enablement/indefiniteness challenges, and challenges based on improper inventorship. Use prior art searches, claim construction, and expert evidence to support invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use and public disclosure (including 35 U.S.C. §273 prior user rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Showing the accused technology was publicly disclosed or in use before the patent filing date can defeat infringement claims or provide a statutory prior-user defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 273: provides a defense to infringement (not invalidity) for commercial internal use occurring at least 1 year before the patent filing; the right has limited scope and is generally not transferable except with the business. Documentation of dates and uses is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct / unenforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent may be rendered unenforceable if there was material misrepresentation or omission during prosecution made with intent to deceive the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-Therasense standard: requires 'but-for' materiality and that the single most reasonable inference from the evidence is intent to deceive. Proof requires showing both materiality and intent; prosecution history, withheld references, and communications with counsel are focal points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud as a defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that the patentee engaged in fraudulent behavior related to the patent can be asserted as a defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraud claims often overlap with inequitable conduct but may involve different factual predicates. Pleading standards and evidentiary requirements are high; factual documentation and timing are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Antitrust defenses assert that enforcement or licensing of the patent involves unlawful anti-competitive conduct that can limit or bar enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include tying arrangements or other conduct that impermissibly extends patent rights. Antitrust allegations may provide both a substantive defense and counterclaims; coordination with economic and market evidence is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied license
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to practice the patent can be implied from the patentee's conduct, such as sale of an unpatented component that is designed to be used in a patented combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof focuses on the nature of the sale and the reasonable expectations of the buyer; document transactions and communications showing authorization or consent to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent exhaustion (first sale doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized first sale of a patented item exhausts the patent holder’s rights to control use of that particular item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an authorized first sale, the patentee cannot assert rights over that specific item; analyze authorization and scope of the sale to determine exhaustion effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited defense for non-commercial experimental research use of patented inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very narrow in the U.S.; generally applies only to purely private, non-commercial activities. Commercial uses or research with commercial intent typically do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair vs. reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchasers may 'repair' a patented item to preserve its useful life but may not 'reconstruct' it (which would amount to making a new patented item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether post-sale activities are restorative (repair) or replacement/re-manufacture (reconstruction); documentation of scope and intent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee impermissibly extends the patent monopoly beyond its lawful scope (e.g., tying arrangements), which can render enforcement improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of misuse require showing that the patentee’s licensing or enforcement practices violated patent-policy limits; remedies and standards vary by jurisdiction and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches / equitable estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable defenses based on excessive delay in bringing suit (laches) or conduct inducing reliance (equitable estoppel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The availability of laches for monetary damages was largely curtailed by SCA Hygiene; analyze timing, prejudice to defendant, and plaintiff conduct for equitable estoppel arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-use defense (28 U.S.C. §1498)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the U.S. government or its contractors use a patented invention, the remedy is an action against the United States under §1498 rather than an infringement action against the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alleged infringer is a government actor or contractor, consider the §1498 remedy and the procedural and substantive implications for damages and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early case assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial evaluation of the merits and risks of a patent suit to guide strategy and resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key tasks: understand the scope of allegations, evaluate potential risks, preserve relevant evidence, and identify weak points in the plaintiff’s case. Early factual and technical investigations (e.g., claim charts, prior art scoping) are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution options (settlement and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Options to resolve disputes outside of a full trial, including negotiated settlements, mediation/arbitration, licensing, and cross-licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cost-benefit, probability of favorable outcomes, enforcement risks (e.g., injunctions), reputation effects, and the potential for cross-licenses when weighing settlement vs. continued litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural strategies / motion practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural tools to shape or dispose of litigation early or limit issues for trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common motions: motion to dismiss (notably §101 subject-matter challenges), motions for summary judgment (non-infringement or invalidity), motions to transfer venue, and motions to stay pending inter partes review (IPR). Use timing and procedural posture to maximize leverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactical approach to obtain, analyze, and use evidence during discovery to support defenses or attack plaintiff’s case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactics include source code review (for software patents), inventor depositions, targeted prior art searches and depositions, and preparation of expert testimony. Preservation and collection of technical and business evidence are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel proceedings strategy (IPR/PGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using post-grant proceedings (IPR/PGR) at the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board in parallel with or as an alternative to district court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: file IPR within one year of the complaint (when applicable), seek stays of district court litigation, and consider estoppel implications of PTAB decisions on later court proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: International/trade remedies (ITC Section 337 investigations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuing or defending Section 337 investigations at the U.S. International Trade Commission as an alternative forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ITC proceedings are generally faster than district court litigation and can result in exclusion orders (customs-based remedies). Consider forum-specific standards and the strategic value of an ITC action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages defenses and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Defenses that limit or reduce monetary recovery, focusing on apportionment and limitations on recoverable royalties and past damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key arguments: apportion damages to the patented feature only, demonstrate non-infringing alternatives, rely on standard/market royalty rates (not enhanced), assert patent-marking requirements under 35 U.S.C. 287, and raise pre-suit damages limitations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful infringement and enhanced damages avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and steps to avoid findings of willful infringement that can expose a defendant to enhanced damages (up to treble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices include maintaining a good-faith belief of non-infringement or invalidity, avoiding willful blindness, documenting due diligence efforts, and obtaining and documenting opinions of counsel when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement considerations and bargaining dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to evaluate when negotiating settlement, license terms, or cross-license arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate litigation costs versus expected outcomes, risk of preliminary injunctive relief, reputational effects, cross-license potential, and relative bargaining power. Use knowledge of plaintiff’s strengths/weaknesses and parallel proceedings posture to inform offers.
